overview: This event ties together hard landings, gear emergencies, and flap failures in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

items.text: Hard Landings is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.

children.text: Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
High Flare
Flare started too early or with excessive pitch-up
Can lead to stalling or nose gear striking runway during pitch correction
Late/Rapid Flare
Final airspeed <110 KIAS increases risk of stall and hard touchdown
Idle or low power (<4-6%) on final + LDG flaps = rapid airspeed decay and high descent rate
The usual trap is missing the setup picture, then trying to salvage Hard Landings late.

items.text: This procedure is used when the landing gear fails to indicate fully up with the gear handle up or fully down with the gear handle down. It’s applicable in situations involving abnormal gear or inboard door positions, and should be used to troubleshoot and determine whether gear indications are safe or if further emergency procedures are required.

children.text: High Temperature / High Pressure Altitude Conditions
(N) Execute this checklist anytime the gear doesn’t indicate fully up or down as expected.
LAMP test switch – Check

LDGGR CONT (left front console), INST (left front console), and INST LT (left rear console) circuit breakers – Check in/reset (If unable to reset the LDGGR CONT circuit breaker, execute the Emergency Gear Extension Checklist)

items.text: Asymmetric (split-flap) condition may cause uncommanded roll or yaw during flap operation. It results from either binding of flap segments or torque link failure between inner and outer flaps. Control authority is sufficient at pattern airspeeds.

children.text: Airspeed – Adjust to maintain control and minimize effort
Flap control handle – Move to minimize/eliminate asymmetry
(W) Once asymmetry is minimized or eliminated, do not reposition flap control handle.
Land – Use straight-in approach
